decision: The unchanged 50/50 expert/replay intervention passes its predeclared replication gate on the two completed valid seeds: seed 0 and seed 1 both have positive target-free current-buffer GAR first-step true advantage (0.500 and 0.406), exceed the fixed expert-only seed-0 parent on decisions-2-to-4 mean advantage (0.094 and 0.115 versus 0.021) and full normalized edit-distance improvement (-1.237 and -1.341 versus -1.745), and retain healthy state effective rank (100.0 and 94.2) and state standard deviation (0.257 and 0.316). Seed 2 is excluded as a process timeout during training, not interpreted scientifically; the gate required at least two seeds including seed 0, so do not finish or seed-scale it. Evaluate the two valid replay checkpoints with an otherwise unchanged four-decision horizon. Conclude that degradation after decision 4 is the immediate bottleneck only if both seeds achieve positive four-step normalized edit-distance improvement under deployment-feasible current-buffer GAR, retain positive mean selected true advantage across decisions 1-4, and beat their matched current-buffer random controls, with all declared artifacts present and no NaNs. If either seed fails, reject simple horizon truncation and next inspect episode-level failure strata before changing training. Proposal generation and GAR selection remain target-free; terminal targets are used only for separately labelled evaluation metrics, and oracle-injected conditions remain privileged diagnostics.
